jobs.description: Position overview Salary range: INTERNAL RECRUITMENT TO UC DAVIS ONLY. The Beckley/Herzog Endowed Chair for Enduring Advancement in the Science of Food provides additional funding to a current UC Davis academic appointee in the Associate Professor, Full Professor or CE Specialist title. The additional funding may support the endowed chair holder in areas of teaching, research, or extension activities directly related to the purpose of the endowment. Application Window Open date: September 24, 2026 Next review date: Monday, Oct 26, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee. Final date: Thursday, Dec 31, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time) Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled. Position description The holder of the Beckley/Herzog Endowed Chair for Enduring Advancement in the Science of Food will be a tenured faculty member or Specialist in the Cooperation Extension (CE) at Associate or Full rank in the Department of Food Science and Technology. The holder of the Chair will be someone who exemplifies excellence in the science of food. Funding will be used to advance excellence in the science of food through innovative teaching, research, outreach, and engagement activities within the Department of Food Science and Technology. The chair is intended to address current and future challenges facing the food system, with particular emphasis on reducing food loss and waste, improving energy and water use efficiency throughout the food system, and advancing biomass utilization. The chair will support scholarship that contributes to a more sustainable, resilient, and efficient food system while strengthening connections among academic, industry, alumni, and public communities. The Chair is for a five-year term appointment and may be renewable based on satisfactory review and at the discretion of the Dean. Responsibilities of the Chair include: • Teach a normal load for the department or provide extension teaching/programs in which the Chair Holder is appointed including student advising and mentoring. • Provide innovation and leadership in research in the area of food systems particularly towards food loss and waste and improving energy and water use within the food systems. • Engage in outreach activities specific to the designated intent by the donor including lectures, conferences, student research. • Perform service to the appointee’s home department and the broader community as expected for faculty at the same academic rank. • Enhance the academic and intellectual life of the campus as a whole. The Chair holder will submit an annual report on the use of the Fund including expenditures of the endowment income to the Dean of the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences each academic year. Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application) • Associate or Full Rank Professor or Specialist in CE in the Department of Food Science and Technology. Preferred qualifications (other preferred, but not required, qualifications for the position) • Teach a normal load for the department or provide extension teaching/programs in which the Chair Holder is appointed including student advising and mentoring. • Someone who exemplifies excellence in the science of food. • Engage in outreach activities specific to the designated intent by the donor including lectures, conferences, student research. • Perform service to the appointee’s home department and the broader community as expected for faculty at the same academic rank. • Enhance the academic and intellectual life of the campus as a whole. Position description Department of English at the University of California, Berkeley is hiring two tenure-track Assistant Professors specializing in pre-1700 English literature. Assistant Professors at Berkeley are expected to excel in research, teaching, and service. Position description Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology Faculty Search The Cardiology Division of the University of California, San Francisco, is seeking a board-certified or eligible faculty candidate in advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology for its growing program. The successful candidate will join a comprehensive, multidisciplinary program that provides the full spectrum of advanced heart failure care, including heart transplantation, temporary and durable mechanical circulatory support (MCS), cardiogenic shock management, and pulmonary hypertension management. Clinical responsibilities include inpatient and outpatient care of advanced heart failure, transplant, and MCS patients; participation in multidisciplinary transplant and MCS patient selection committees; and teaching and mentoring of medical students, residents, and fellows, including trainees in the ACGME-accredited Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology fellowship. Qualifications • Education & Rank: Must hold an MD, MD/PhD, or MD/MPH degree and qualify for appointment at the Instructor, Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank. • Clinical Training: Formal fellowship training in both inpatient and outpatient management of advanced heart failure, heart transplantation, temporary and durable mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices, and pulmonary hypertension. • Board Certification: Board certification or eligibility in Cardiovascular Disease and in Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology (ABIM). • Licensure: Possession of, or eligibility for, a medical license in the State of California. Position description Assistant (Tenure-Track) Professor in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE) Faculty Position in Aero/Space Structures The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of California, Irvine (UCI) is inviting applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor rank, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. The rapidly evolving landscape of aerospace engineering, driven by advances in next-generation aircraft, urban air mobility, hypersonic and high-speed vehicles, and ambitious space initiatives such as NASA’s Artemis program, the United States Space Force, and the growing commercial space sector, calls for pioneering innovations in aerospace and space structures. Future air and space platforms will demand structures that are lighter, stronger, more adaptable, and more efficient than conventional approaches allow, spanning applications from high-performance airframes to deployable, in-orbit, and lunar/planetary structures.. To address these challenges, UCI’s Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering seeks exceptional applicants with demonstrated potential to become a leader in aero/space structures. Areas of Interest span experimental, computational, and theoretical thrusts and include: • Advanced structural concepts for air and space platforms, including deployable, reconfigurable, and morphing structures (origami- and kirigami-inspired, thin-shell composite, and tensegrity concepts), in-space manufacturing, and in-space/in-field robotic, modular, and autonomous assembly and repair of large-scale structures. • Aerospace structures leveraging advanced composites and additive manufacturing, including AI-driven strategies for manufacturing, computational design and optimization, and adaptive or multifunctional structures with integrated actuation and sensing. • Structural mechanics and life-cycle assessment of aircraft and spacecraft structures with emphasis on materials behavior and characterization, including fatigue, fracture, and damage tolerance, aeroelasticity, and structural health monitoring across airframe and space-structure applications with extreme thermal, mechanical, and/or dynamic loading. • Emerging structural challenges in hypersonic, reusable, and autonomous platforms, including thermal-structural and aerothermoelastic response, and resilient, rapidly manufacturable structures for next-generation defense and space missions. • Structural dynamics of large, flexible, and ultralight space structures, including pointing-error mitigation under attitude-control maneuvers. For full consideration, applications should be submitted by December 15, 2026. This position will remain open until filled. Apply online at recruit.ap.uci.edu/JPF10461. Position description The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of California, Irvine invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in multidisciplinary design and optimization (MDO), with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We seek outstanding candidates advancing the theory, computation, and application of MDO for complex engineering systems, with particular emphasis on aerospace applications and AI-driven approaches. Advances in machine learning, high-performance computing, and digital engineering are reshaping how complex aerospace systems are designed. Design cycles that once proceeded sequentially, discipline by discipline, can now be posed as a single coupled problem, so that structural integrity, thermal management, aerodynamic performance, and propulsion efficiency are optimized simultaneously rather than reconciled after the fact. Areas of primary interest include AI-integrated aerospace vehicle design; digital engineering and autonomous system optimization; surrogate modeling for complex aero-thermal systems; and data-driven flight dynamics. Related areas include optimization of coupled multiphysics systems, reduced-order modeling, design under uncertainty and robust or reliability-based optimization, and model-based systems engineering. Candidates developing broadly applicable methodologies are encouraged to apply regardless of the specific application domain in which their work has been demonstrated. The successful candidate will establish a high-impact, externally funded research program; teach and mentor students at the undergraduate and graduate levels; and contribute to the intellectual life of the department and the profession. The position will strengthen the department’s systems and design area and provide opportunities for collaboration across dynamics and controls, fluid dynamics and propulsion, mechanics of materials and structures, and thermal and transport sciences, as well as across the Samueli School of Engineering and Southern California’s aerospace and technology community. Applications should be submitted at http://recruit.ap.uci.edu/JPF10462, the UCI Recruit portal. Documentation Required: Curriculum Vitae, Cover Letter, Statement of Research, Reflective Teaching Mentoring Statement, Publications (three publications or manuscripts), References (contact information only - 3 required). Reference letters will be requested at a later stage of candidates under serious consideration. Applications received by December 16, 2026 will receive full consideration. Applications will continue to be accepted until June 30, 2027, but those received after the review date will be considered only if the position has not yet been filled. Position description Berkeley Law is one of the nation’s great centers for legal education, ever exploring and pushing new intellectual boundaries while tackling urgent, real-world issues. The law school is also known for its vibrant and engaged community of students and scholars who are committed to providing leadership and making a difference on problems of local, national and global import. Currently ranked among the top law schools in the country, the School of Law has ambitious development goals as it looks to continue producing leaders in law, government, and society. Berkeley Law invites applications for a full-time position on our clinical faculty, teaching in our Death Penalty Clinic. This faculty position entails membership in the Academic Senate with rights and responsibilities that are comparable to the standard professorial track, but with an emphasis on teaching, professional competence and activity, research and creative work, and University and public service. Berkeley Law's Clinical Program includes seven in-house clinics: Environmental Law Clinic, Death Penalty Clinic, Global Rights Innovation Lab Clinic, Human Rights Clinic, Policy Advocacy Clinic, Samuelson Law, Technology & Public Policy Clinic, and Social Enterprise Clinic. The program also partners with the East Bay Community Law Center to offer community-based clinics: the Clean Slate Clinic, Community Economic Justice Clinic, Consumer Justice & General Clinic, Youth Defense Clinic, Education Justice Clinic, Health & Welfare Clinic, Housing Law Clinic, and Immigration Law Clinic. The Death Penalty Clinic is dedicated to developing students' advanced legal advocacy skills while providing exceptional legal representation to individuals facing capital punishment. In response to the critical shortage of qualified and adequately funded counsel for people on death row, the clinic represents clients primarily in post-conviction proceedings, with a particular focus on jurisdictions that have the fewest legal resources. The clinic also tackles problems endemic to the administration of capital punishment. Through this work, students gain intensive, hands-on experience in complex litigation while contributing to high-quality representation in cases involving the most serious criminal penalties. The mission of Berkeley Law’s Clinical Program is to advance equal justice - racial, economic, and social justice - through three interrelated activities: preparing law students to address pressing societal problems and to become highly skilled, responsible, and reflective legal practitioners; providing first-rate legal services to underrepresented individuals, marginalized communities, and public-minded organizations––locally, nationally, and globally; and producing cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research to support litigation, inform public policy, and increase the effectiveness of our teaching and service. Berkeley Law strives to educate responsible, effective, and forward-thinking advocates who serve the public through legal practice, public policy, academic scholarship, and related fields. In doing so, the school addresses some of society’s most pressing challenges by leveraging its strengths in teaching and research to improve law, policy, and public institutions. Position description Position Description: The University of California, Berkeley invites applications for an approved faculty position at the non-tenured (tenure-track) Assistant Professor level in the area of AI for Materials. This appointment will start as a 100% Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) appointment, with the appointee joining the Bakar Institute for Digital Materials for the Planet (BIDMaP) in the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS) as a member, with access to its collaborative resources and postdoctoral program. It is the intention to move to the position to a 50/50 split appointment between MSE and a future interdisciplinary data science unit if/when established in CDSS, with MSE as the home department. About the Units: The MSE department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and maintains close ties with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). It advances the understanding and design of materials through an interdisciplinary blend of chemistry, physics, and engineering, pairing rigorous fundamentals with modern, application-driven approaches. Our key strength is our collaborative, cross-disciplinary research community, with abundant opportunities for students and collaborators across campus and beyond. BIDMaP is an institute in CDSS, a new college at Berkeley, with the goal of advancing the state-of-the-art in the core of computing, data science, and statistics, while making sustained progress on issues of human and societal significance. BIDMaP advances the synthesis, design, and translation of innovative materials aimed at mitigating critical global challenges. Through the integration of pioneering chemistry with machine learning, artificial intelligence, and robotic automation, BIDMaP transforms materials innovation into targeted solutions for clean air, clean water, advanced batteries, and sustainable chemical production. About the Position: We seek outstanding candidates demonstrating the potential to build a world-class research program that uses and advances AI to enable transformational progress in materials science and engineering. Research may span the development of new AI methods motivated by materials challenges, co-development of emergent AI with materials theory and experimentation, and the deployment of AI to accelerate materials research, discovery and innovation. Position description The School of Information at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank. Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a field of expertise focused on the evolving relationship between people and computing systems. HCI researchers design and study new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with technology, and investigate how emerging computing systems shape human capabilities, practices, organizations, and society. Methods include the design and development of novel systems, experimentation, qualitative and ethnographic research, participatory design, computational methods, field studies, and mixed-methods research. We seek applicants who are defining the next generation of human-computer interaction: developing new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with increasingly intelligent computing systems. We are particularly interested in scholars who both imagine and build new forms of human-computer interaction and rigorously investigate how these technologies shape people, organizations, and society. This broad, interdisciplinary field can include the study of literary history, social history, intellectual history, religious history, or linguistic history. Additional areas of specialization that would be welcome are Portuguese, Arabic, Hebrew, Latin, Catalan, Occitan, Mediterranean Studies, gender studies, race studies, and material culture studies. Position description The Berkeley School of Education invites applications for a tenure track position at the assistant professor level in the area of Civics Education, with a focus on civic learning and democratic engagement. We welcome applicants from education as well as a range of connected disciplinary and interdisciplinary spaces, including but not limited to political science, public policy, history, ethnic studies, and data science. The candidate should have research, publication, and teaching and/or mentoring experience in Civics Education with undergraduate and graduate students appropriate to rank. Preference will be given to scholars whose work centers K–12 classrooms and youth civic development. The applicant’s research focus should explore the teaching and learning of civics and advancing learning theory to address the challenges and possibilities of public democratic life. Across the United States and globally, young people express deep concern about polarization, misinformation, civic exclusion, and the fragility of democratic institutions. We seek a scholar whose research program explores Civics Education in ways that respond to these realities and who designs innovations that help educators meet the needs, interests, and aspirations of students. Given the increasing importance of digital citizenship, information literacy, and the civic implications of technology, we would expect the candidate to have some expertise in these areas. About UC Berkeley School of Education In the Berkeley School of Education, we educate like democracy depends on it– because it does. In a fast-changing, polarized world where inequalities and existential threats multiply, education remains an essential lynchpin for fostering human potential, achieving generational progress, and nurturing civic engagement. Together our research, teaching, and practice supports a vision of public education that has as its goal equity and inclusion at all levels - classroom, school, community, district, state, nation, and globe. Our students arrive with exceptional academic talent and professional experience, driven to make a meaningful impact as researchers, educators, leaders, and innovators. Together, faculty and students engage with pressing questions, from how children, youth, and adults learn across varied contexts, to how schools, communities, and societies can expand opportunities and advance educational equity. Through effective and equity-informed education, the BSE helps people and communities learn to dialogue across difference, use critical thinking to make informed decisions, and advance both individual achievement and progress for the benefit of society. As a world leader in public education, guided by a commitment to excellence in scholarship, teaching, innovation, and leadership, our professional and academic programs help prepare the next generation of educators, leaders, scholars, and policymakers, while contributing to transformative knowledge creation and the public good. Advances in quantum computing, sensing, and communications increasingly hinge on engineered semiconductor platforms, heterogeneous integration, and the device/circuit infrastructure that connects quantum hardware to scalable systems. Position description The Department of Film and Media Studies at UC Santa Barbara invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Media Industries and AI. We seek a scholar whose research and teaching examines artificial intelligence as a media industry phenomenon, including its infrastructures, labor, political economy, regulation, and cultural, artistic, and social implications. We welcome candidates working on any global region and through any critical, historical, or empirical methodology, including but not limited to production studies, platform and infrastructure studies, science and technology studies, critical algorithm studies, political economy, labor studies, cultural and industrial history, and creative or practice-based research on generative media. We are especially interested in candidates who can speak to one or more of the following: the restructuring of film, television, gaming, digital media, and/or music industries by AI systems; the labor of AI production, from data annotation to creative and technical work displaced or transformed by automation; the environmental, material, and geopolitical infrastructures underlying AI; algorithmic culture, recommendation systems, and platform governance; or the aesthetics, authorship, and cultural politics of generative and synthetic media. This position calls for a humanities-based, critical, media industries approach to the study of AI—one attentive to history, culture, power, embodiment, and meaning-making, rather than a purely technical or computational orientation. The faculty of the Department of Film and Media Studies engages in scholarship and pedagogy across multiple scholarly approaches, fostering a dynamic and expansive understanding of film and media study. With this appointment, we seek to extend the department’s scholarly and curricular strengths and advance our department’s commitment to diverse, interdisciplinary research and teaching. Position description The Department of Plant Pathology in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Plant Pathology with an emphasis on plant health and microbiomes. This is an academic year (9-month), tenure-track Assistant Professor position that includes an appointment in the California Agricultural Experiment Station (AES), with responsibility for research and outreach relevant to the AES mission, as well as university service. The appointee is expected to establish a competitive, externally funded research program in plant microbiome science that addresses critical and emerging issues in plant pathology. The program should advance microbiome-informed approaches to the diagnosis, prediction, and/or management of plant diseases and develop science-based solutions to promote plant health. Research should generate fundamental and applied understanding of the composition, function, and/or dynamics of plant-associated microbial communities (including bacteria, fungi, oomycetes, viruses, and/or other microorganisms) and their interactions with plant hosts and each other. Areas of interest may include disease-suppressive microbiomes, dysbiosis and pathobiomes, host-microbiome-pathogen interactions, pathogen-pathogen and pathogen-nonpathogen interactions, disease complexes and multi-infections, microbiome engineering, synthetic communities, and the ecology and evolution of pathogens within the phytomicrobiome. Research may also address climate-driven changes in plant-microbiome interactions and emerging diseases, span model, agricultural, and/or natural plant systems, and should have a strong mechanistic and/or predictive foundation. The appointee will complement existing departmental strengths in plant-microbe interactions, disease epidemiology, and disease management, while expanding microbiome-informed approaches relevant to food security, agricultural sustainability, climate resilience, and the broader One Health framework. The appointee will be expected to teach GDB103: The Microbiome of People, Animals and Plants, a 3-unit, upper-division undergraduate course that serves Global Disease Biology (GDB) and other students. The appointee is also expected to contribute to required GDB courses, such as GDB90: Introduction to Global Disease Biology, GDB 187: Global Disease Biology Seminar, and PMI129Y: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces, and will have opportunities to contribute to graduate courses such as PLP201B: Ecology and Epidemiology of Plant Pathogenic Organisms and PLP298: Microbial Ecology. Training and mentoring of graduate students, undergraduate student advising, curricular development, outreach, and departmental and university service are expected. The successful candidate will be an active member of the Plant Pathology Graduate Program and other graduate groups as appropriate and will have opportunities to collaborate with Cooperative Extension specialists and advisors, relevant industries, and other public stakeholders. This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant Professor rank, and the resulting appointment will be at that rank regardless of the appointee's qualifications.

Position description POSITION AVAILABLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Teaching in Epidemiology QUALIFICATIONS: The Weill School of Veterinary Medicine (WSVM) at UC Davis seeks an interdisciplinary Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Teaching in Epidemiology to advance its veterinary education and research mission through pedagogy of epidemiology in veterinary sciences. Professor of Teaching faculty are Academic Senate faculty members whose expertise and responsibilities center on instruction and scholarly activities in their field or involving pedagogy. The appointee will teach courses delivered by SVM in related programs that may include undergraduate teaching, teaching in the DVM curriculum, and in the Graduate Groups in Epidemiology and Master of Preventive Veterinary Medicine. Example courses could include courses in basic and advanced epidemiology, public health, vector and infectious disease epidemiology, disease ecology, and biostatistics. The selected candidate must have the ability to teach advanced, quantitatively rigorous material such as advanced epidemiology and applied statistics. The appointee is expected to lead five to eight courses per year as relevant to the Weill School of Veterinary Medicine in professional, graduate, and/or undergraduate programs. An advanced graduate degree (PhD required) in epidemiology or related field, with experience in teaching as an instructor of record or lecturer, is required. A veterinary medical degree (DVM or equivalent) is preferred. The successful candidate must have expertise in epidemiological methods and biostatistics. They must demonstrate successful application of epidemiology in collaborative settings involving topics such as causal inference, population health study design, bias reduction, risk factor analyses, clinical algorithm development, disease surveillance, disease ecology, intervention evaluation, etc. Competence in an appropriate programming language (e.g. SAS, R, Stata) is required. A documented scholarly record or potential to develop innovative scholarly activities in veterinary epidemiology and/or pedagogy is required. Demonstrated excellence in teaching is required for appointment at the Associate or Professor rank, as is evidence of engaging students with limited prior mathematical training. Evidence of leadership skills is required. The individual must possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to work with others in a collegial atmosphere. Preferred qualifications include documented success in the following areas: teaching large classes of 150 or more students, use of evidence-based teaching practices, use of modern instructional technologies, and the ability to identify and develop effective teaching strategies for varied levels of learner expertise in epidemiology. Research experience in animal and/or vector epidemiology and ability to teach advanced epidemiologic methodology (e.g., causal inference, counterfactual theory, methods for assessing heterogeneity of effects or sources of bias) are preferred. Position description Associate Dean for Graduate Medical Education Position Summary The Associate Dean for Graduate Medical Education (GME) and Designated Institutional Official (DIO) serves as the senior institutional leader responsible for the strategic direction, oversight, accreditation, quality, and continuous improvement of Graduate Medical Education programs. Reporting to the Vice Dean for Education, the Associate Dean/DIO provides vision, leadership, and operational oversight for all accredited and non-accredited residency and fellowship programs sponsored by the institution and serves as the institution’s official representative to the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME). The Associate Dean/DIO partners closely with department chairs, program directors, faculty, health system leadership, affiliated training sites, and learners to ensure excellence in clinical education, trainee well-being, patient safety, and professional development. The position requires deep expertise in graduate medical education administration, accreditation, educational innovation, and organizational leadership. Key Responsibilities Institutional Leadership and Strategy Provide strategic leadership for all Graduate Medical Education programs and initiatives at UCSF and the UCSF Fresno regional campus. Develop and implement a vision for GME that aligns with the institution’s educational, clinical, research, and community missions. Advise the Dean, Vice Dean for Education, and health system senior leaders on matters related to graduate medical education. Lead institutional efforts to anticipate and respond to evolving trends in medical education, healthcare delivery, workforce development, and accreditation requirements. Promote innovation, educational excellence, and continuous quality improvement across all residency and fellowship programs. Designated Institutional Official (DIO) Responsibilities Serve as the institution’s Designated Institutional Official as defined by ACGME Institutional Requirements. Maintain institutional accreditation and ensure compliance with all ACGME requirements. Provide oversight of the Sponsoring Institution and all ACGME-accredited programs. Chair or oversee the Graduate Medical Education Committee (GMEC) and ensure effective governance of GME programs. Monitor program quality, accreditation status, and institutional performance metrics. Lead institutional reviews, accreditation site visits, annual reporting, and responses to accreditation actions. Ensure appropriate oversight of participating sites and educational partnerships. Educational Leadership Provide leadership for the design, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of graduate medical education curricula. Support residency and fellowship program directors in achieving educational excellence. Foster innovation in competency-based education, assessment, coaching, and learner development. Promote integration and alignment across undergraduate medical education, graduate medical education, and continuing professional development. Support faculty development initiatives related to teaching, mentoring, assessment, and educational leadership. Quality, Safety, and Learning Environment Promote a culture of patient safety, professionalism, accountability, and continuous learning. Ensure residents and fellows are appropriately engaged in quality improvement and patient safety initiatives. Position description The Department of Psychology and the Department of Urban Planning and Public Policy (UPPP) in the School of Social Ecology at the University of California, Irvine, invite applications for a joint tenure-track faculty position at the Associate Professor level in Behavior Change, Decision Science, and Policy. The position will advance research on how individuals and groups make decisions, change behavior, and respond to interventions, institutions, and public policy. We seek scholars who connect behavioral science to important real-world problems with a strong commitment to translating research into effective interventions, actionable programs, and policy solutions. The successful candidate will complement the Department of Psychology’s strengths in basic and applied behavioral research (spanning developmental, health, social, or clinical domains) as well as UPPP’s focus on public policy, inequality, social problems and environmental issues. Interdisciplinary Research and Policy We welcome scholars whose research examines behavior change and decision-making––such as motivation, beliefs, social influence, self-regulation, and risk perception––and connects them to policy design, practice, and broader societal outcomes. We are particularly interested in candidates who bridge individual-level psychological science with social, institutional, community, or environmental contexts. The successful candidate will advance an interdisciplinary agenda that explores both how policy shapes human behavior and how behavioral insights can optimize the design, evaluation, and translation of public interventions and policies. This joint appointment offers rich opportunities for collaboration across Psychology, Urban Planning and Public Policy, the School of Social Ecology, and the broader UC Irvine campus. Teaching and Mentoring The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in Psychology and UPPP. Teaching may include courses addressing behavior change, decision-making, behavioral science, public policy, urban planning, and/or the candidate's substantive area of expertise. The candidate will mentor students across disciplinary boundaries and contribute to preparing students to apply psychological and behavioral science to complex social and policy problems. Qualifications Candidates must have a doctoral degree in psychology, public policy, urban planning, or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates should demonstrate: a strong or emerging independent research program; expertise in behavior change, decision science, behavioral science, policy, or a related area; a strong foundation in psychological or behavioral science; potential for interdisciplinary research and external funding commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring; and commitment to service to UCI and the academic profession. Candidates whose work bridges behavior change, decision-making, and public policy are particularly encouraged to apply. Position description The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Associate/Full Professor of Agricultural Economics. This is an academic year (9-month), tenured Associate/Full Professor position with a 20% Instruction and Research (I&R), and 80% Agricultural Experiment Station (AES) appointment. The appointee is expected to establish an outreach and research program in agricultural economics, with a focus on the issues facing California’s farm economy. The appointee will bolster our applied research footprint across the state and help meet the needs of California's agricultural sector through applied research on agricultural production costs and returns, farm-level costs and impacts of regulation, and of management strategies that strengthen profitability and long-run economic viability. The successful candidate is expected to oversee UC Davis ARE's world-renowned Cost and Return studies program (Cost and Return Studies). This will involve supervising research staff, engaging with funders and external stakeholders, as well as maintaining an extramural granting program to support core programmatic activities and methodological improvements. Teaching responsibilities will consist of one to one-and-a-half quarter-long courses per year. The courses to be taught by the appointee will be set by the department chair based upon departmental needs and the successful candidate’s interests/expertise. The appointee’s primary teaching responsibilities are likely to include ARE 120 Agricultural Policy, ARE 138 International Commodity & Resource Markets, 139 Futures & Options Markets, and/or ARE 155 Operations Research & Management Science. Other courses that the appointee may be asked to teach include MS level courses in agricultural economics and finance (ARE 223, ARE 271), and PhD level courses in empirical methods (ARE 202B, ARE 202C), and agricultural economics (ARE 231, ARE 232, and ARE 233). Other responsibilities include student advising at the graduate and undergraduate levels, and training/mentoring graduate students. Performance of departmental and university service at the level commensurate with a tenured faculty member is expected. This recruitment is being conducted at the Associate/Full rank. The resulting hire will be at the Associate or Full rank depending on the proposed appointee's qualifications. This is an academic year (9-month), tenured position that includes an appointment in the California Agricultural Experiment Station (AES). Faculty members who hold an AES appointment have a responsibility to conduct research and develop new knowledge and technologies that address specific problems of importance for the people of California. Position description The UCSF Department of Neurological Surgery and The Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology are jointly recruiting a faculty member at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level to lead a new research program supported in part by the UCSF Brain Tumor Center, focused on immunotherapy for brain tumors. The successful candidate will be a basic scientist based at the Gladstone Institutes (Mission Bay), with primary faculty appointment in the Department of Neurological Surgery. Candidates must have a strong background in immunology, genomics, genetics, genome engineering, and/or synthetic biology, and significant achievements and meaningful promise in developing novel immunotherapies for brain tumors. We invite applications from scientists with Ph.D., M.D./Ph.D., or equivalent degrees who are establishing or have established an independent basic science research program in brain tumor immunotherapy research. Relevant areas of research include, but are not limited to: Genome engineering to enhance adoptive cellular therapies for brain cancer Protein design and engineering in the context of the immune system and immunotherapies for brain cancer Systems immunology and immunotherapy in neuro-oncology Preclinical disease models and clinical translation of innovative immunotherapies in the context of the brain Investigators will be expected to develop extramurally sponsored research programs and educate, mentor, and develop graduate and medical students. The successful candidate will hold a primary faculty appointment in the UCSF Department of Neurological Surgery, along with an Investigator affiliation at the Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology, as an Assistant, Associate or Full Professor, and will be assigned dedicated research space, primarily located in new Gladstone Institutes space at Mission Bay, with additional support from the UCSF Brain Tumor Center. About Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology To harness the immense potential offered by immunotherapies, the Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology combines emerging biomedical technologies at the intersection of human immunology, genomics, CRISPR genome engineering, computational biology, and synthetic biology. The institute’s scientists deepen knowledge of how DNA sequences control cell functions in the human immune system. Their discoveries will enable the next generation of immunotherapies for cancer, autoimmune diseases, infectious diseases, inflammation and beyond. This institute is the result of a close partnership between Gladstone Institutes and the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). With wet and dry lab space to be housed (starting in 2027) in a new building on the Mission Bay campus, it creates a unified community across the two campuses and combines UCSF’s world-class immunology and planned cell therapy efforts with Gladstone’s expertise in the host-pathogen interface, iPS cells, computational biology, and CRISPR gene editing technologies. Within our overarching advancing health worldwide mission, UCSF is devoted at every level to serving the public. Position description The School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences at the University of California, Irvine, is seeking a Chairperson to lead the Department of Clinical Pharmacy Practice. The Chair reports to the Dean and provides leadership for the department's teaching, research, clinical, and service missions while also holding a faculty appointment as either an Associate/Full Professor of Clinical Pharmacy Practice (Clin X) or a tenured Associate/Full Professor. This posting is for the Clin X series; the related tenured faculty posting is available here: JPF10389. Applicants should apply to the series that best aligns with their qualifications and experience. Only one individual will be selected to serve as Department Chair, and there is no preference between the Clinical X and tenured applicant pools. Faculty appointment will be made at a professorial rank commensurate with the candidate's academic qualifications and experience. The Department of Clinical Pharmacy Practice offers unparalleled training for future careers in pharmacy, preparing students both in the classroom and in clinical settings to improve the health and well-being of society. Its 20 faculty members conduct collaborative research across a broad range of areas, including clinical trials, medication adherence, pharmacokinetics, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenomics, pharmacoeconomics, pharmacy practice, and outcomes research. Clinical X faculty are members of the Academic Senate but are not supported by state funds. They are expected to engage in scholarship, teaching, clinical activities, and service to the University (see APM 275f). Research expectations differ somewhat from those of ladder-rank faculty. Clinical X faculty are expected to lead or make significant intellectual contributions to research programs and/or other creative activities. These activities may be closely integrated with clinical practice and may include clinical and translational research, health services and outcomes research, case series, educational scholarship, or bench research. Extramural funding is desirable but not required. Teaching responsibilities may include classroom and laboratory instruction, with an emphasis on clinical education for PharmD students. Applicants must hold either an M.D. or M.D/ Ph.D. degrees, with either a current California medical license or eligibility for California medical licensure, and be board certified in Clinical Pathology (CP), Anatomic & Clinical Pathology (AP/CP) or Infectious Disease (ABIM-ID). Position description The Department of Film & Digital Media at the University of California, Santa Cruz (UCSC) invites applications for the tenure-track position Assistant Professor of Narrative Film and Media Production. We are seeking applicants whose innovative creative work demonstrates an active and sustained practice in narrative form, expansively defined, with expertise in moving image media, production, and exhibition. Building on the department’s well-established strengths in documentary film and media, social justice-centered approaches to creative practice, and work that critically and creatively engages emerging technologies, we are particularly interested in candidates whose work bridges narrative and documentary practices, engages community-based and collaborative methods, or explores evolving modes and technologies of production. We welcome candidates whose work engages in a broader range of media practices, including interactive, participatory, and immersive media. The position will require the assistant professor to maintain an active creative research practice with a record of exhibition in festival, theatrical, streaming, or broadcast contexts. Our campus follows a schedule of three 11-week quarters per academic year. Our department values interdisciplinary scholarship and practice, and we are interested in candidates who can further expand the skillsets and modalities that we can offer our students. Further responsibilities of the position encompass advising and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, engaging in faculty governance at both departmental and campus levels, and actively partaking in administrative service for the department, the affiliated college, and the university as a whole. Position description In-Residence Faculty Position – Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry University of California, San Francisco The UCSF Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry in conjunction with the Cardiovascular Research Institute (CVRI) seeks faculty active in synthetic chemistry and/or chemical biology to join our vibrant, collaborative, and supportive discovery research community at the Mission Bay Campus in San Francisco. The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry includes diverse research in the areas of computational and synthetic chemistry, biophysics, chemical biology, peptide and protein design, systems and synthetic biology, enabling technologies, and drug discovery. Our department is characterized by a culture of collaboration and innovation in biomedical science: Faculty members typically have positions in one or more of our graduate groups (e.g., Chemistry & Chemical Biology, Biophysics & Computational Biology). The CVRI is devoted to fundamental research with direct or indirect relevance to cardiovascular disease. We seek creative, innovative scientists who define and address fundamental questions in chemical biology. We are particularly interested in chemists, who wish to build a program that blends organic synthesis with biochemical, computational, and analytical methods to probe biological mechanisms. We provide faculty with resources to launch their program, including a strong mentoring culture, a competitive start-up package, administrative support, and facilities for advanced computation, organic synthesis, light and cryo-electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, high-throughput small molecule screening, cytometry, and state-of-the-art animal care. Position description The UCLA CMRS Center for Early Global Studies is pleased to announce a John W. Baldwin Post-Doctoral Fellowship for a recent Ph.D. whose work focuses on European medieval studies within the global comparative context. The position is for a maximum of 2 years, beginning July 1, 2027. To be eligible for consideration, applicants must have received their Ph.D. between September 1, 2020, and June 30, 2027. The Post-Doctoral Fellow will be a scholar whose research aligns with the goals of the study of “Europe in the world” and who has demonstrated evidence of innovative methodologies. A successful applicant may be working in a discipline or between disciplines in the European Middle Ages but should engage Europe in the world at micro and macro levels. We understand the European Middle Ages to include the period from the 3rd to the start of the 17th century, and where the 16th century is studied in continuity with the late medieval period. Mirroring the work of John W. Baldwin, for whom the postdoctoral fellowship is named, a successful applicant will conceive of Europe within a broader global context and be conversant across disciplines. The Fellow will join the vibrant research and academic communities within the CMRS Center for Early Global Studies, with scholars working on all facets of early Global studies. He/she/they will have the following responsibilities and opportunities: develop their research agenda while participating regularly in CMRS-CEGS academic events; work collaboratively with a diverse group of scholars, graduate students, and other postdoctoral fellows; help to conceive Center’s programming (including public-facing programming). He/she/they will have the opportunity to prepare one scholarly event (workshop or small symposium) hosted by CMRS-CEGS in the second year. Named to honor the legacy of the esteemed historian JOHN W. BALDWIN, this postdoctoral fellowship is made possible by a gift from Arcadia, a charitable fund that works to protect nature, preserve cultural heritage and promote open access to knowledge. We are seeking to interview candidates with a demonstrable commitment to underrepresented and underserved populations and epistemologies, and with an enthusiasm for building ties across fields within the university. The appointment (which includes benefits) will be for a 24-month period. Salary will follow university standards for post-doctoral scholars and will reflect the applicant’s experience. Qualifications Basic qualifications • Ph.D.; must have been awarded doctoral degree between September 1, 2020, and June 30, 2027 • Research specialization in relevant field Additional qualifications • Commitment to cross-disciplinary and collaborative research • Proven track record in designing and completing research assignments • Ability to translate research findings into publishable research and public-facing formats Application Requirements Document requirements Curriculum Vitae - Updated CV detailing both academic and professional achievements, including doctoral degree completion and any prior postdoctoral experience. Position description The University of California, Santa Barbara seeks a highly motivated postdoctoral scholar to lead a new research program examining how wildlife communities respond to the rapidly expanding wildland-urban interface. As development increasingly borders and fragments natural habitat, an important set of ecological and conservation questions is emerging: How do animal communities change across the transition from relatively intact wildlands to developed landscapes? Which species tolerate or exploit edges, and which are displaced by them? Do protected lands adjacent to development function as refuges, foraging habitat, or movement corridors? How do human-associated resources alter wildlife behavior and food webs? Can strategically-protected habitat at the wildland-urban boundary help sustain ecological communities while reducing negative interactions between wildlife and people? This research will address these questions in the Santa Barbara foothills surrounding Los Padres National Forest, an area of mountain wildlands abutting developed coastal landscapes. Specific research questions will be developed collaboratively with the successful candidate, who will have substantial intellectual freedom to shape the scientific direction of the project. Example research questions may include: ● How do vertebrate species richness, community composition, and activity change across gradients of human development? ● Which species are most sensitive to wildland-urban edges, and which species benefit from or tolerate them? ● Does wildlife activity become increasingly nocturnal near residences and other human activity? ● How do responses to development differ among mammals, birds, bats, amphibians, and other vertebrate groups? ● How do wildlife responses to developed edges change seasonally or during periods of drought and resource limitation? ● Do protected areas at the wildland-urban boundary function primarily as habitat, refuge, foraging areas, or movement corridors? ● How does proximity to development alter wildlife diets and trophic interactions? ● When and why do wildlife begin relying on human-associated foods, ornamental vegetation, commensal prey, or other anthropogenic resources? ● More broadly, what characteristics make protected lands at the wildland-urban interface most effective at maintaining biodiversity and ecological function? The project will be designed to integrate multiple complementary approaches. Position description The Goulding Lab at UC Irvine, in collaboration with the Hayes Lab at UC Santa Barbara, is seeking a postdoctoral scholar with expertise in cryo-electron microscopy to investigate the molecular mechanisms of bacterial competition. Position description A postdoctoral position is available in the laboratory of Dr. Rebecca Tarvin in the Department of Integrative Biology and the Museum of Vertebrate Zoology at the University of California, Berkeley to study the genetic and physiological basis of kleptocnidy in nudibranch mollusks. The Department of Integrative Biology (IB) is a dynamic group of researchers answering important questions in evolutionary, ecological and functional biology in an interdisciplinary collaborative environment. IB shares rich connections with four natural history museums, and is a leading force in promoting field research and educational opportunities. We address problems relevant to human health and origins, the diversity of life, and biological interactions at all scales. Research in the Tarvin Lab focuses on the genetic and physiological adaptations of animals to naturally occurring toxins. The Tarvin Lab is also based in the Museum of Vertebrate Zoology, a leader in studies of biodiversity and evolution. Please visit our website for more information about our research and the lab. This position is being hired as part of an NSF-funded project in collaboration with Jessica Goodheart at the American Museum of Natural History to study the process of kleptocnidy, the theft and storage of microscopic stinging structures (nematocysts), in nudibranch mollusks. We are interested in whether this unique process evolved through specialization of phagocytosis, an ancient cellular process used across animals for immune defense and intracellular digestion. The role of the postdoctoral scholar will be to identify the molecular processes underlying kleptocnidy in Californian nudibranchs using RNA-sequencing and pharmacological inhibition assays. The position duties include, but are not limited to: Carry out original scientific research related to dietary theft in nudibranchs, including animal husbandry, genomics, molecular biology, physiology and field work within the U.S. International field work is an opportunity that may arise during the course of employment. Write and publish peer-reviewed papers and other scholarly material on the results of the research. Present scientific results at professional meetings, scientific institutions, and, when appropriate, to the media and popular audiences. The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to develop new projects in the context of our research program. Position description Do you want your AI research to move beyond benchmarks and make an impact in real-world healthcare? UCLA’s Center for Advanced Surgical and Interventional Technology (CASIT), part of the Department of Surgery at the David Geffen School of Medicine, is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Scholar with strong expertise in computer vision, multimodal AI, machine learning, and/or agentic AI to help build the next generation of intelligent digital health solutions. You will work side by side with clinicians, engineers, researchers, and industry partners to transform multimodal health data—including wearable and sensor data, medical images and video, speech, human movement, physiological signals, and clinical information—into AI-powered tools for digital biomarkers, remote monitoring, precision health, clinical decision support, and intelligent surgical systems, with the ultimate goal of translating AI innovation into measurable improvements in patient care. About the Role: We are looking for a researcher with a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Data Science, Robotics, Computational Health, or a closely related field and a strong record in AI, machine learning, digital health, or biomedical data science. You will lead interdisciplinary projects that apply advanced computational methods to clinically meaningful problems across the continuum of care—from early detection and functional assessment to intervention, surgery, recovery, and monitoring at home. Prior clinical experience is not required; scientific curiosity, strong quantitative skills, and a genuine interest in learning from clinicians and solving real-world healthcare problems are essential. What You Will Work On: Depending on your strengths and interests, projects may include: Digital biomarkers and multimodal health assessment: Develop AI models that integrate wearable sensors, movement, speech, physiological signals, imaging, video, and clinical data to characterize health status, frailty, resilience, cognitive-motor function, and disease progression. Wearables and remote monitoring: Transform longitudinal data from wearable and connected technologies into clinically actionable measures for monitoring patients in the hospital, at home, and in the community. jobs.description: Position overview Salary range: Starting $71,491 Review timeline: For full consideration in the first review of applicants, materials should be submitted by November 30, 2026. Position description Fusion Energy represents one of the grand challenges for humankind, offering the prospect of limitless baseload electricity, an inherently safe configuration, with no significant greenhouse gases or nuclear waste. As a thriving fusion industry develops multiple promising concepts for fusion, it is vital to look ahead to solutions for continuous energy production. Thus, UCLA seeks to pioneer the steady state tokamak as a concept in its own right, and as a tensioner to drive the development of the many constituent science and engineering components of the challenge, that will drive broader benefits to the fusion field. To this end, UCLA is establishing a Fusion Simulation Center to develop concepts for a compact fusion power plant that integrates foundational discovery plasma science, fusion science and engineering. The explicit goal is the development of robust and cost-effective configurations overall for fusion in steady state, as well as innovative approaches and advanced solutions in each of the technical fields and systems comprising a power plant. This work will thus serve as an integrating focus of a very broad range of activities across Engineering and Science at UCLA from energy extraction, blanket design, tritium breeding, and materials development to fundamental plasma science and efficient energy-confining plasma configurations. Thus, the Department of Physics & Astronomy at UCLA seeks outstanding candidates as a postdoctoral scholar in the area of Fusion Simulation. Key responsibilities and tasks will include: Using simulation suites to develop optimized configurations for fusion power plants or other fusion testbed devices. Writing software modules to address specific facets of this challenge. Undertaking investigations into particular aspects of the power plant solutions (could range from fundamental discovery or fusion plasma science questions to technology aspects such as facets of blanket design or materials behavior, depending on skill of applicant. Support to other users as needed, including students and student projects in the center. Generate scientific deliverables including journal papers and conference talks. Pursuing collaborative engagement within UCLA and or other key partners to investigate particular issues and approaches. Potentially to engage in, or collaborate with validation exercises such as experimental tests on tokamaks or other testbed devices. The successful candidate is expected to be able to operate with autonomy and grapple with highly complex technical issues, distilling them down to essential understanding for a working knowledge. Qualified candidates will have a Ph.D. in Physics or a related field, 3+ years experience and a demonstrated background directly applicable to the tasks, including experience with fusion simulation activities on the science or engineering side. Specific understanding of relevant plasma science or fusion technology is essential, but may be weighted to the plasma science and/or fusion technology side. Candidates should provide a curriculum vitae; a publication list; a Statement of Research Interests and Future Research Goals, complete a reference check authorization release form, and arrange for 2-3 letters of reference to be uploaded to UCLA Academic Recruit by November 30. Qualifications Basic qualifications Ph.D. in plasma physics or a closely related fusion technology

The detector concept is a Fabry-Perot Michelson interferometer with an optically trapped micro-disk in each arm cavity. Position description The UCSB Department of Communication is recruiting for a tenure-track/tenured open rank faculty position. Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming how humans communicate, coordinate, and organize across workplaces, institutions, and society. AI increasingly shapes organizational decision-making, collaboration, knowledge production, expertise, and identity while reconfiguring power, authority, accountability, and the boundaries between human and machine agency. These developments create new opportunities to revisit foundational organizational communication theories while also demanding new theoretical and empirical approaches to understanding AI as a sociotechnical actor embedded within organizational and institutional systems. We seek a scholar who conducts innovative, theoretically grounded, and empirically rigorous research using quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-method approaches that addresses the social consequences of AI from an organizational communication perspective. This could include, but is not limited to, topics such as human-AI collaboration; algorithmic decision-making and governance; sustainability; visibility and surveillance; ethics and corporate social responsibility; power and inequality; and (dis)empowerment of underrepresented groups. We are particularly interested in scholarship that advances organizational communication theory by examining how algorithms or algorithmic systems reshape communication processes, organizing practices, and institutional change, rather than only treating AI as a methodological or analytical tool. We anticipate that the faculty hire will make meaningful connections and engage in multidisciplinary endeavors across campus such as the Mellichamp Initiative in Mind & Machine Intelligence, the Department of Technology Management, the Center for Information Technology & Society’s research foci in AI, the Pahl Center for the Study of Critical Social Issues, and campus-wide initiatives in AI and related communities of practice. UCSB is ranked among the top public universities in the United States, and the Department of Communication is also highly ranked in worldwide comparisons. UCSB is a designated Hispanic Serving Institution, and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution. It offers several programs to support incoming faculty, including housing assistance (Faculty Housing | Campus Housing) and various grant support programs. Wen School of Population and Public Health, invites applications for a full-time tenure-track or tenured faculty position in health policy within the Department of Health, Society, and Behavior (DHSB). We invite applications at the Assistant or Associate level in health policy with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We seek a scholar with strong training in health policy or a closely related field whose research examines how policies, institutions, social conditions, and behavioral and economic processes shape health or health care. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: health policy; health care delivery systems and organizations; health services research; health economics, insurance, and financing; health care access, quality, and outcomes; the health effects of social policy and social determinants of health; and health equity and disparities. The successful candidate is expected to have a theoretically grounded and methodologically rigorous research program that advances the field of health policy and contributes to the broader research mission of the Department of Health, Society, and Behavior. We welcome a range of methodological approaches, including quantitative and qualitative methods, mixed methods, policy analysis, health economics, longitudinal and population-based approaches, and research that integrates multiple levels of analysis. We are particularly interested in scholars whose work connects health policy with the social determinants of health, health disparities, health behaviors, or interventions at the population level. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active program of research with strong potential for extramural funding; teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students; and help shape and expand the area of health policy within the Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health through leadership and service. This is a state-funded, 9-month position. The current teaching load in the Department of Health, Society, and Behavior is two 4-credit courses per academic year, including at least one core undergraduate course in public health or health care policy and one graduate course. Graduate teaching will contribute to the MPH Health Systems and Policy concentration, which covers health politics, health care payment and delivery, health policy analysis, health economics, and evaluation, with an emphasis on evidence-based approaches to improving health care and public health systems; and the PhD program in Health, Society, and Behavior, which examines the social, structural, and behavioral determinants of health and health inequities through basic, applied, and community-engaged research. The successful candidate will be part of the Joe C. Wen School of Population and Public Health and will have opportunities to collaborate across the university and with researchers in public health, medicine, nursing, biological sciences, social sciences, and related fields and centers. The department values collaborative and interdisciplinary scholarship and seeks scholars whose research will contribute to understanding how health policies and social contexts influence health and health equity. Students will conduct research, develop concepts, build prototypes, test their ideas, respond to critique, and communicate their work. This is not a traditional lecture-based UX/UI course. Position description Department of Visual Arts at UC San Diego invites applications for an Assistant Professor of Teaching in Film and Media Studies. The Assistant Professor of Teaching will teach in the quickly growing interdisciplinary Cinematic Arts major and will collaborate with The Suraj Israni Center for Cinematic Arts. This center promotes research, scholarship, teaching, production and exhibition of film, providing access and opportunity for UC San Diego students and scholars to pursue instruction in cinematic arts. We seek a candidate who is working across a range of potential research areas, including film and media history, theory, aesthetics, and curation. The ideal candidate will bring a rigorous approach to foundational film studies while engaging adjacent fields like time-based media, experimental and expanded cinema. This candidate will provide a crucial role in performing the pedagogical mission of the Cinematic Arts major. Duties include classroom teaching at all levels, graduate supervision, active research, and departmental and university service. The successful candidate will teach in the Department of Visual Arts undergraduate Media major, an area spanning analog and digital photography, film, digital media, and the history, theory, and criticism of film and media. The position also entails teaching in the M.F.A. program and contributing to the Ph.D. programs in Art History, Theory, and Criticism and Art Practice. We seek candidates whose research, teaching, and service records demonstrate their capacity to contribute to culturally responsive pedagogy, engaging with students from all social backgrounds. Our ideal candidate will demonstrate a commitment to inclusive teaching of non-traditional, global, or marginalized cinematic perspectives. Teaching will encompass the entire curricular range, from large undergraduate lecture courses to graduate courses for MFA and Ph.D. Art Practice students. Courses could include such topics as Histories of World Cinema, Second Cinema, Third Cinema, the Avant-garde in Cinema, Documentary Film History, Media Art Histories and the Aesthetics of Cinematic arts. All department faculty are expected to advise, work with, and serve on the committees of, MFA students in all areas and also work with, and serve on the committees of, Ph.D. students. The Department of Visual Arts ranks among the world’s leading art schools. Founded on the principle that the production, critical analysis and history of art are inter-related activities. The Department of Visual Arts offers undergraduate degrees in Art History, Studio Art, Media, Speculative Design, and the Interdisciplinary Computing in the Arts Major (ICAM), as well as housing internationally renowned graduate programs in studio art (MFA) and art history and art practice (PhD).
